description:
You have a Java project called 'commons-cli' (Apache Commons CLI library) open in Eclipse. This project is NOT currently under version control — there is no .git directory.

Your task is to use Eclipse's EGit integration to:

1. Initialize a Git repository for this project (Team > Share Project > Git).
2. Create a .gitignore file in the project root that excludes at minimum:
   - target/
   - *.class
   - .settings/
   - .classpath
   - .project
3. Stage all project files for commit (drag to Staged Changes).
4. Make an initial commit with EXACTLY this message: "Initial commit: Import Apache Commons CLI library"

IMPORTANT:
- Use Eclipse's built-in Git support (EGit) accessible via the Team menu.
- The project is located at /home/ga/eclipse-workspace/commons-cli/.
- Do NOT push to any remote — just make a local commit.
- Make sure build artifacts (target/ directory, .class files) are excluded via .gitignore BEFORE committing.
- The .gitignore file itself should be included in the commit.
